subject: Finova: EU gateway 503/504 wave — feedback-loop causing sustained 5xx/429
messages:
From: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@finova.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: priya.das@finova.com, alerts@finova.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:12:30Z
Subject: Re: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Hi Naomi,

We just saw a sudden wave of 503/504s across our EU endpoints starting ~08:05 UTC. User traffic to our payments flow is experiencing timeouts and elevated retry loops; calls that normally succeed in <200ms are timing out after 30s. Our side is seeing exponential retries being sent back into your region (we've attached a short trace and a dashboard screenshot).

This is impacting transactions for several of our merchant partners. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's edge or proxy layer and whether you have an active mitigation plan we can share with our SREs? This is priority P1 for us — we need visibility and a timeline.

Thanks,
Lucas
SRE Lead, Finova Bank

Attachments: eu_edge_503_wave_dashboard.png (screenshot), proxy_connection_trace.txt (log excerpt)
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@finova.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:20:12Z
Subject: Re: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Lucas — thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm escalating internally now. Initial triage: our EU LB fleet reports increased 5xx and a surge in short-lived TLS connections; some proxies are hitting connection limits and returning 502/503 to downstreams, which can amplify client retries.

Immediate actions we are starting now:
- Temporarily enable more aggressive circuit breakers on the EU edge (limit concurrent upstream connections per origin).
- Increase our prefix/KV cache TTL on common authorization paths to reduce upstream calls where safe.
- Apply a rule to drop high-frequency client retries at the edge (de-dupe within 3s) to break the retry feedback loop.

I'll loop Marcus (runtime) and Grace (ops) for ETA and to confirm fallbacks to a lower-capacity variant that tolerates retries better. We will produce an incident timeline and a mitigation note for your SREs within 30 minutes.

— Naomi
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:28:01Z
Subject: Re: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Thanks Naomi. Quick notes from runtime:
- Observed sudden connection churn against the EU proxy pool starting 08:03 UTC. Most failures are 502/503 from proxy->upstream timeouts; upstreams appear healthy but are overwhelmed by bursty retry traffic.
- We can flip an autoscale burst on the EU gateway for the next 60 minutes; will take ~3 mins to spin additional pods.
- Circuit-breaker and drop-retry rules are staged and ready; will push them sequentially to avoid cascading failovers.

Plan:
1) Push drop-retry filter at 08:32 UTC (edge config)
2) Engage autoscale burst 08:34 UTC
3) If errors persist, route 20% of traffic to a lower-latency path (regional fallback) at 08:40 UTC

Marcus
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:33:45Z
Subject: Re: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Pushing the drop-retry rule now to 50% of edge nodes for test; I'll monitor 1-min error rate and queue depth. If we see error-rate drop by >30% within 5 minutes, I'll roll to remaining nodes. Also starting autoscale burst (requested) — estimating 180s to availability.

Heads-up: prefix cache TTL bump approved for auth checks — doing a conservative 30s extension to avoid staleness.

Grace
Head of Cloud Ops, Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@finova.com>
Cc: priya.das@finova.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-22T08:45:05Z
Subject: RE: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Lucas — update from our side: we have deployed an edge-level retry de-dupe filter and enabled an autoscale burst for the EU gateway. Early telemetry shows a ~40% drop in 5xx within the first 8 minutes; queue depth on the proxy layer is decreasing.

Next steps we recommend on your side to reduce noise and speed recovery:
- If possible, throttle client-side retry backoff to linear 3s for the next 30 minutes.
- Avoid client-side synchronous fanout during the window.

We're keeping the mitigation live and will provide a full timeline + postmortem. Sharing an internal mitigation plan document to your drive link now.

— Naomi
From: Lucas Meyer <lucas.meyer@finova.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, priya.das@finova.com
Cc: alerts@finova.com
Date: 2026-11-22T09:05:12Z
Subject: Re: Production — EU region gateways spiking 503/504

Naomi / team — thanks for the fast response and the clear next steps. We've adjusted our client retry policy and disabled synchronous retries in the payments flow. Error rate is trending down from our dashboard as well.

Two asks for the follow-up:
1) Can Redwood confirm whether the root cause appeared to be connection saturation at the proxy (TLS session churn) vs an upstream bottleneck? We need wording for our internal incident report.
2) Please keep the circuit-breakers and drop rules in place until we get a formal green from both sides.

I'll keep monitoring and let you know if anything regresses.

Lucas
